record_selection: every public record of each system (calibstats.load_dataset_dir without a cap): 6554 records, 521-713 per system; per-trajectory statistics use at most 40 records per record kind inside compute_all

rules.pos: [min / 2, 2 x max] (a factor-2 margin on both sides of the real range)

check_rule: compare(): a checked statistic is ok when the fraction of synthetic systems inside target_range is >= min_inside_frac, the suite's [min, max] overlaps the real [min, max], and the coverage condition (suite min <= a, suite max >= b) holds when given.
coverage_rule: coverage [a, b] (the suite must contain a system with value <= a and one with value >= b), for statistics whose two real classes form two regimes: with 'low' the class with the smaller median, a = the low class's maximum rounded UP to one significant figure and b = the high class's minimum rounded DOWN to one significant figure; if a >= b (the classes overlap), a and b are the two class MEDIANS rounded the same way, with a at least 0.01

classes.full: a full recurrent network (about 200 observed units, 9-20 readout units, one input)
classes.mechanism: a small candidate sub-circuit (3-6 observed units) of such a network, with the same readout and input

dependence_classes.system: a property of the system's own dynamics under nominal conditions; the intervention design changes it little
dependence_classes.design: set mainly by the experimental design (magnitudes, onsets, durations, initial conditions, input schedules, record mix); comparable only between data built with the same design
dependence_classes.mixed: a system response whose value also scales with the design

labels: anonymous labels, the same system-to-label assignment as in the earlier file
source: PUBLIC real-system trajectories only, built with the benchmark's dataset design v2 (LOG P4-D36): passive sets (nominal input over parameter draws, input schedules, restarts from nominal passive trajectories for initial-condition variability, structural weight noise), reference interventions (single-target kicks, current pulses and temporary silencing on public targets, four magnitude classes, onsets in the first half of the trajectory) each with its counterfactual twin, public validation and test items, and pool-source trajectories. No explicit initial states, no hidden data, no hidden targets, no evaluation output.

records_per_system.large: 521 (40 passive + 120 reference interventions + their 120 twins + 9 passive and 24 intervention validation records + 24 twins + 24 test interventions + 24 twins + 16 passive tests + 120 pool sources)
records_per_system.small: 713 (the same with 200 reference and 40 validation interventions)

design.intervention_kinds: single-target kicks, current pulses and temporary silencing (no persistent silencing)
design.magnitude_classes: below / weak / moderate / strong = 0.1 / 0.3 / 1 / 3 x a moderate magnitude per kind, jittered by 0.8-1.25 (strong never above 3 x); silencing has no magnitude; a kick clipped at the floor is labelled by its realized size
design.onsets: uniform in [0.15, 0.5] of the trajectory duration
design.initial_states: no explicit initial states (setting a unit's initial value is a kick at t = 0): initial-condition variability comes from 'obs.init' restarts at 25-90 % of a nominal passive trajectory of the same parameter draw; the pools' 'init' sources restart from the first (nominal) source of their draw
design.input_levels: 0.55-1.45 of the nominal input, including multi-step schedules
design.structural_noise: multiplicative weight noise with sd up to 0.1
design.twins: every intervention record has a counterfactual twin with the same parameters, initial condition (rest or restart source) and input and no event; twins keep their item's integration pieces (no-op input breakpoints at the event times)

note: Computed from the public real data built with the benchmark's OWN dataset design, version 2 (no explicit initial states; initial-condition variability from restarts of nominal trajectories; LOG P4-D36), the design that also builds the synthetic tiers, so a synthetic suite built by the same design is directly comparable. Supersedes calibration_targets_v2_explicit_init_design.json (design v1: explicit initial states on half the observed units), which in turn superseded calibration_targets_v1_earlier_design.json. Statistics marked 'design' or 'mixed' (dependence.class) depend on the design; the change columns compare with version 2.
caveats: Design dependence: effect sizes, near-zero-effect shares, signal-to-noise ratios, kick sizes, peak rates and the noise floor are set largely by the design (magnitude classes, initial conditions, twin integration). Compare them only with data built by the same design; system-property statistics (spectra, autocorrelation, onset latency, relaxation times, single-trajectory dimensionality, rectification, readout participation) are comparable across designs.

The public trajectories are deterministic simulations. Twins share their item's integration pieces, so the pre-event difference is exactly 0 and the noise floor is the float32 storage resolution (1.2e-7 of the rate scale); observation noise is a benchmark parameter, not a property of the real systems.

Initial-condition variability now comes from restarts of nominal trajectories: the share of 'obs.init' records that end in a persistent high-activity state is 0 % in the large systems and 0-11 % in the small ones (init_high_state_frac_x). In version 2 the explicit initial states moved two of the three large systems into that state in about 70 % of the records, which set their rate scales (s_x, s_y) and every statistic normalised by them.
Current magnitudes are in the simulator's input units; their relation to a unit's threshold is not published, so only their effects are calibrated.
Single-unit time constants are not published; persistence is estimated from the kicked unit's own decay (self_decay_s).

effect_energy_outside_passive95 is above 0 in every system (0.43-65 %). In version 2 it was 0 in the four small systems with 3 observed units: with the explicit initial states, their passive 95 % subspace spanned every observed direction.
Oscillation: every real system oscillates (6.8-17 Hz). The autocorrelation decay is then about a quarter period, not a memory time.
Ten systems in two classes are few; the recommended ranges widen the real range by a stated rule rather than fitting it.
